page.title: New spaces
page.description: Proposed new recreational and educational amenity in the Glenabo and Corrin catchment, described in four phases.

hero.title: Two projects in early development.
hero.intro: Both sit inside the action area of about 990 hectares. Neither is agreed yet, and both are described here as proposals rather than plans.

items.title: Corrin moorland
items.text: Upland habitat on the Corrin side of the action area, outside the Glenabo catchment but part of the same walk and the same landscape.

items.title: Corrin wetlands
items.text: Wet ground with potential for habitat creation and for holding water back before it reaches the main channel.

blocks.heading: The proposed route
blocks.text: The phased approach runs from interpretation on existing trails through to a single connected loop.

items.label: Phase 1
items.heading: Glenabo interpretation
items.text: Trail signage with codes linking to ecology, biodiversity, flora, fauna, folklore and history, and to guidance on responsible recreation.

items.label: Phase 2
items.heading: Corrin interpretation
items.text: The same approach applied at Corrin, reflecting its own ecological, archaeological and landscape character.

items.label: Phase 3
items.heading: Glenabo extension
items.text: Roughly 600 metres of new trail to the rear of the existing route, reaching a forest track opposite the road to Waste Recovery Services.

items.label: Phase 4
items.heading: The full loop
items.text: Linking Glenabo to Corrin to give a connected route of up to 15 km, joining Fermoy Quays, Barnane, Glenabo Woods, Corrin Woods and the Cork Road.

blocks.text: Any works would be subject to Coillte consent, environmental assessment including screening for Appropriate Assessment where required, and compliance with health and safety standards.
